To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The detrimental effects, particularly on the system efficiency and MPTT performances, of the voltage oscillations of the DC-link of double-stage grid-connected PV systems are evidenced.

the use of a proper compensator acting on the error between a reference signal and a signal proportional to the PV voltage is able to improve the MPPT performances of double-stage grid-connected PV systems.
the detrimental effects of the PV voltage oscillation on the system performances can be effectively mitigated by the proposed compensation network.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the interactions between the MPPT controller, the DC/AC converter, and the DC/DC converter of a double-stage grid-connected PV inverter.
the development of an improved MPPT control strategy for double-stage grid-connected PV systems that is able to improve the system performances and the MPPT performances.
the study of the dynamic interactions among MPPT controllers and DC-DC converters, which can lead to a deterioration of the performances of grid-connected photovoltaics systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed technique allows to improve the MPPT performances of double-stage PV systems, in terms of efficiency and of the tracking speed, without any additional cost and without any need for any additional sensor.
the proposed approach allows the MPPT performances of double-stage PV systems to be significantly improved, with a very simple and low cost implementation.

the proposed approach is able to improve the performances of the double-stage PV inverter system, in terms of both system efficiency and MP PT performances, with respect to the conventional P&O MP PT algorithm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed approach is a simple, effective, and low cost technique to improve the MPPT performances of double stage grid-connected PV systems.

the proposed compensation network allows the MPPT controller to operate in an ideal condition, i.e., the MPPT algorithm is able to track the maximum power point (MPP) even in the presence of the PV array oscillations.
a novel technique is presented to enhance the MPPT performances in double-stage photovoltaic (DPV) grid-connected systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a proper control technique can improve the performances of double-stage grid-connected PV systems, in particular the MPPT ones.
the MPPT controller of a double-stage grid-connected inverter should be properly tuned in order to achieve the best system performances.
a proper design of the compensation loop can significantly improve the system performances in terms of efficiency and dynamic response.
